_description: P0 eval-corpus, category: slide-decks. Source doc: Stephen Jones, 'CUDA: New Features and Beyond', GTC 2024. Extended 2026-05-21 from the rigorous baseline (15→30 queries) to give P2.x A/Bs statistical signal. New queries cover NVRTC compilation, kernel fusion, NVLink C2C, CUTLASS abstractions, LU factorization, performance-per-watt thesis, and unified memory. Extended 2026-05-23 with 3 chart-content queries (31-33) targeting content exclusively in chart-extracted blocks (the P3.3 v7 unlock).
_mix: 20 answerable (17 prose + 3 chart-content) + 5 empty-retrieval refusals + 8 near-miss refusals
_labelling_rule: For each answerable query, run `memex search --k 10`; `relevant_chunk_ids` = every chunk in the top-10 whose text contains the literal answer (or equivalent paraphrase). Single-chunk labels appear when only one chunk has the answer text; multi-chunk labels appear when the chunker's overlap creates near-duplicate chunks.

queries.question: What is the energy cost of FP16 matrix multiplication relative to FP32, in FMA operations?
queries._expected_answer: 0.5x (from the Energy per FLOP table for matrix multiply)
queries._note: Re-labelled with broader chunk set after the initial bootstrap revealed chunk-set-equivalence under-labelling.

queries.question: What are the two main categories where modern processors spend power, according to the slides?
queries._expected_answer: 1. Data movement, 2. Computation
queries._note: Genuinely single-chunk answer; the low rerank (0.029) is a retrieval-quality finding to surface, not a labelling issue.

queries.question: How does the power cost of floating point arithmetic scale with the mantissa length?
queries._expected_answer: Power of floating point arithmetic generally scales as the square of the mantissa length.

queries.question: What changed about transistor density and power efficiency between 2004 and 2022, per the TSMC chart?
queries._expected_answer: Transistor density grew massively (120x), but transistors got less power-efficient over the same window; the deck calls out this divergence as the energy-efficiency motivation.

queries.question: Why is data movement a key concern for power efficiency in modern processors?
queries._expected_answer: Modern processors spend significant power on data movement (one of the two categories of power consumption); reducing it is one of the headline strategies in the deck.
queries._note: Single-chunk answer (top-10 search confirms no other chunk discusses data movement as a power factor). Borderline rerank score useful for threshold testing.

queries.question: What is the energy cost of FP8 tensor core matrix multiplication relative to an FP32 FMA?
queries._expected_answer: 0.06x (from the Energy per FLOP table; Tensor Core MMA in FP8).

queries.question: Which floating-point format has a 5-bit exponent and 10-bit mantissa?
queries._expected_answer: half (FP16) — listed in the precision sign/exponent/mantissa diagram.

queries.question: In what year did NVIDIA acquire Mellanox?
queries._expected_answer: (Refuse — the deck is about CUDA architecture, not corporate M&A history.)

queries.question: What is the recommended chunk size for retrieval-augmented generation pipelines?
queries._expected_answer: (Refuse — RAG is unrelated to a CUDA architecture deck.)

queries.question: What is the manufacturer's suggested retail price of the NVIDIA RTX 4090?
queries._expected_answer: (Refuse — pricing is not discussed in this technical deck.)

queries.question: What is the energy cost of FP128 matrix multiplication relative to FP32, in FMA operations?
queries._expected_answer: (Refuse — the Energy per FLOP table covers FP64/FP32/FP16/FP8/Int8 but not FP128.) This should pull the precision-table chunks at high rerank but the agent should recognise FP128 is absent.
queries._note: Tests near-miss refusal: retrieval will route to the FP-precision chunk which is the right neighbourhood, but the specific value asked isn't there.

queries.question: What is the FP4 tensor core energy cost per FLOP relative to an FP32 FMA?
queries._expected_answer: (Refuse — the table lists FP8 as the smallest tensor-core precision; FP4 is not in this deck.)
queries._note: Same chunk-neighbourhood as the precision-table answerable queries; tests whether the agent grounds on the specific value or hallucinates by analogy.

queries.question: What is the NVLink bandwidth between Hopper and Blackwell GPUs?
queries._expected_answer: (Refuse — Grace-Hopper bandwidth is discussed but Blackwell isn't covered in this 2024 deck.)
queries._note: Pulls the NVLink-bandwidth chunks; the agent must distinguish Grace-Hopper from a non-existent Hopper-Blackwell pairing.

queries.question: How many CUDA cores are in NVIDIA's latest data-center GPU according to this deck?
queries._expected_answer: (Refuse — the deck discusses transistor density and SM architecture but does not list CUDA core counts.)
queries._note: Tests whether the agent over-claims about GPU specs based on architecture-discussion chunks.

queries.question: What is the kernel-fusion speed-up factor for converting FP32 to INT8 according to the slides?
queries._expected_answer: (Refuse — kernel fusion is discussed but the example given is FP32→FP16, not FP32→INT8.)
queries._note: Tests whether the agent substitutes the FP32→FP16 example as if it answered the FP32→INT8 question.

queries.question: By how much has NVRTC compilation time improved since CUDA 11.8 for a hello-world kernel?
queries._expected_answer: 6x speedup since CUDA 11.8 (from the NVRTC compile-time chart).

queries.question: In the deck's basic kernel-fusion example, how many kernel launches does the unfused FP32→FP16 multiplication require versus the single fused version?
queries._expected_answer: 3 kernel launches unfused vs 1 launch fused.

queries.question: What is the NVLink C2C bandwidth between the Grace CPU and Hopper GPU?
queries._expected_answer: 900 GB/s NVLink C2C.

queries.question: Which two programming-language abstractions does CUTLASS provide for tensor cores?
queries._expected_answer: C++ and Python abstractions.

queries.question: What new NVRTC flag reduces front-end compilation time by excluding rarely-used compile-time-expensive features?
queries._expected_answer: The '-minimal' flag.

queries.question: How much lower are the overheads of the NVRTC '-minimal' flag compared to the default '-O3'?
queries._expected_answer: 1.6x lower overheads than default '-O3'.

queries.question: What method does the deck describe for getting IEEE-754 FP64-accurate results from FP16 tensor cores?
queries._expected_answer: Mixed-precision LU factorization with GMRES iterative refinement: do the LU factorisation in FP16 on tensor cores, then refine in FP64 until accurate enough.

queries.question: What does the Grace-Hopper unified memory address space refer to in the deck?
queries._expected_answer: Two memory systems (Grace LPDDR5X + Hopper HBM) presented as one address space accessible by both CPU and GPU.

queries.question: What is the energy cost of an FP16 Tensor Core MMA matrix multiply relative to an FP32 FMA?
queries._expected_answer: 0.12x (from the Energy per FLOP table; Tensor Core MMA in FP16).

queries.question: What is the deck's central thesis about the right performance metric to optimise in modern accelerators?
queries._expected_answer: It's about performance per watt (the section is titled '_It's about Performance per Watt_').
queries._note: Borderline rerank score (0.26) — the answer is the deck's THESIS, captured in section heading. Useful test of whether the agent grounds on heading-level structural signal.

queries.question: What is the mantissa length of an FP4 number in this deck?
queries._expected_answer: (Refuse — the precision-bit table covers FP64/32/16/8/Int8 mantissa lengths but FP4 is not in the table.)
queries._note: Sister near-miss to slide-decks-12 (FP4 tensor core cost). Tests whether the agent extrapolates a mantissa value by analogy with FP8 (3-bit) when FP4 is absent.

queries.question: What is the NVRTC compile time for hello-world in CUDA 11.0?
queries._expected_answer: (Refuse — the NVRTC chart shows speedups SINCE CUDA 11.8; CUDA 11.0 is not present.)
queries._note: Tests whether the agent extrapolates a value from the chart's domain. Should refuse because 11.0 is outside the chart's range.

queries.question: What is the maximum latency of NVLink C2C between the Grace CPU and Hopper GPU?
queries._expected_answer: (Refuse — bandwidth is given (900 GB/s), but latency is not.)
queries._note: Tests whether the agent substitutes bandwidth for latency. The bandwidth/latency confusion is a common LLM near-miss failure.

queries.question: What is the thermal design power of the NVIDIA H100 reference design?
queries._expected_answer: (Refuse — TDP / cooling specs are not in this architectural deck.)

queries.question: What programming language must I use to write CUDA kernels — only C++, or are other options supported?
queries._expected_answer: (Refuse — although Python interfaces are mentioned for some libraries, the deck does not give a comprehensive answer to 'which languages can write CUDA kernels'.)

queries.question: What four design principles does the nvmath-python architecture figure highlight?
queries._expected_answer: Minimal lead-time, Inter-operability, Pythonic library interface, Platform-agnostic
queries._note: CHART-TARGETED (P3.3 v7 follow-up). Content exists ONLY in the chart-extracted block from the nvmath-python architecture figure. Should answer under Docling+chart-OCR+v7 stack. Anchor unresolvable via FTS by design (chart blocks stripped from BM25).

queries.question: What duration is shown for the CameraGestureBase_accumulate_values operation in the Nsight Systems timeline figure?
queries._note: CHART-TARGETED. Duration appears only in the chart-extracted Nsight timeline table (the v7 LaTeX→markdown converter put it in a markdown table). Anchor unresolvable via FTS by design.

queries.question: Per the nvmath-python architectural figure, which existing Python numeric libraries does it interoperate with?
queries._expected_answer: NumPy, SciPy, CuPy, PyTorch, scikit-learn, scikit-image
queries._note: CHART-TARGETED. The library list exists ONLY in the chart-extracted block of the nvmath-python architecture figure. Anchor unresolvable via FTS by design.
